# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the

34	# TASK A — the ch13-return reset is a story-world reclaim, and the mechanism is now proven
35	
36	**The generic same-system handoff WORKS. It commits to Origin. The chapter world
37	binding then reclaims the departure world one render later, and the ship
38	controller re-seats the ship on the hearth pad.** This is not a parked ship, not
39	an unready shell, not an aim cone, not a speed budget.
40	
41	## The one line that causes it
42	
43	`main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts:128-131`
44	
45	```ts
46	const CROSSING_DESTINATION_WORLD_ID: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
47	  'ch8-crossing': TIDEGARDEN_WORLD_ID,
48	  'ch10-ask': STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID
49	};
50	```
51	
52	`'ch13-return'` is **absent**. Its own docstring (`:118-127`) describes this exact
53	failure for chapter 10 — "the ship relaunched, crossed, was reclaimed, and
54	relaunched again, eighteen times over, and `activePlanetId` could never leave the
55	sibling" — and the boot resolver's comment (`:88-96`) even says ch13-return "is
56	owned by the world it launches from, **exactly as ch10-ask is**". `ch10-ask` is
57	listed in the runtime map. `ch13-return` was not. Chapter 13's *landed* beats
58	(`ch13-survey`, `ch13-common`) were correctly added to the boot resolver's
59	`originOwnedBeat` set at `:97-99`; only the in-flight beat's runtime entry was
60	missed.
61	
62	Identities (`main/src/game/starSystem.ts:90-94`, slot 0 has no `:pN` suffix):
63	`STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID = '-1,-1'` = **Origin** (destination);
64	`TIDEGARDEN_WORLD_ID = '-1,-1:p1'` = **hearth/departure**.
65	
66	## Executed reproduction (CPU-only, shipped module, no game change)
67	
68	`verifier/probes/handoff-standby-audit/resolver-repro.mjs` bundles the *shipped*
69	`main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts` out-of-tree with the repo's own esbuild and
70	calls the real exports in node. Output —
71	`logs/handoff-standby-audit/resolver-repro.log`:
72	
73	| case | beat | currentWorld | activePlanetId | `resolveStoryRuntimeWorldId` | verdict |
74	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
75	| pre-handoff | ch13-return | `-1,-1:p1` | `-1,-1:p1` | `-1,-1:p1` | stable |
76	| **post-handoff (committed)** | **ch13-return** | **`-1,-1`** | **`-1,-1`** | **`-1,-1:p1`** | **SWAPS BACK** |
77	| post-landing | ch13-survey | `-1,-1` | `-1,-1` | `-1,-1` | stable |
78	| post-landing | ch13-common | `-1,-1` | `-1,-1` | `-1,-1` | stable |
79	| **control** | **ch10-ask** | **`-1,-1`** | **`-1,-1`** | **`-1,-1`** | **stable** |
80	| control | ch8-crossing | `-1,-1:p1` | `-1,-1:p1` | `-1,-1:p1` | stable |
81	
82	This is an **executed** result on shipped code, not a traced branch. The ch10-ask
83	control is identical committed state and is protected; ch13-return is not.
84	
85	## The runtime chain (traced from source, corroborated by measured telemetry)
86	
87	1. `App.tsx:1264-1298` `beginPreparedSystemTargetHandoff` → `onMidpoint` calls
88	   `commitSystemPlanetHandoff({worldId:'-1,-1', renderOrigin:[0,0,0]})`
89	   (`state/systemFlight.ts:203-232`), `enterAtmosphere()`, and
90	   `setCurrentWorld(Origin)`. Its story gate at `:1268-1271` passes because the
91	   Tidegarden route is online. **The generic path is not the problem.**
92	2. `App.tsx:537-545` recomputes `storyRuntimeWorldId` on the next render. With
93	   `ch13-return` missing from the table it answers `-1,-1:p1`, so
94	   `storyWorldSwapPending` is true.
95	3. `App.tsx:622-634` (the story-world swap effect) fires:
96	   `setPreviousWorld` → `resetSceneReady()` → `setCurrentWorld(hearth)` →
97	   `setArrivalMode('surface')`.
98	4. `EfficientScene.tsx:744` passes `activePlanetWorldId={commandContext.world.worldId}`
99	   — now the hearth again — into `ShipController`.
100	5. `ShipController.tsx:459-477`: same `systemId`, so the interstellar branch is
101	   skipped and the `else if` at **:472-473** runs
102	   `setActiveSystemPlanet('-1,-1:p1')`, then re-acquires the pose lease and
103	   republishes `planetLocalPoseToSystemPose(boarding pad, hearth position)` at
104	   **:476-478** — the ship is back on the pad.
105	
106	## Why the second mutator is *proved*, not guessed
107	
108	The commission forbade asserting an unproven mutator. Telemetry
109	`logs/flight-discriminator/telemetry.jsonl` at the first boundary (perfMs
110	41 110 → 41 400, one 290 ms gap):
111	
112	```
113	41110  ep3  local_space  active -1,-1:p1  target -1,-1  renderOrigin [2180,-110,-1635]
114	41400  ep5  atmosphere   active -1,-1:p1  target null   renderOrigin [0,0,0]
115	       pose [2187.9,-58.5,-1643]  (hearth boarding pad)
116	```
117	
118	- `renderOrigin` is **`[0,0,0]` = Origin's system position**, with
119	  `locationMode:'atmosphere'` and `target:null`. Only
120	  `commitSystemPlanetHandoff` (`systemFlight.ts:214-224`) produces that exact
121	  triple. **The Origin handoff demonstrably executed** (epoch 3→4), which also
122	  answers the discriminator's open question: a transient
123	  `activePlanetId === '-1,-1'` existed inside the unsampled gap.
124	- Epoch 4→5 returns `activePlanetId` **and** `lastActivePlanetId` to `-1,-1:p1`
125	  while `renderOrigin` **stays `[0,0,0]`**. Of the only three mutators that can
126	  change `activePlanetId`, `commitSystemPlanetHandoff` would have rewritten
127	  `renderOrigin` to the hearth's position and `resetSystemFlightForInterstellarArrival`
128	  would have rewritten `renderOrigin` and `systemId`. Neither did. Only
129	  `setActiveSystemPlanet` (`systemFlight.ts:189-200`) leaves `renderOrigin`
130	  untouched while setting both ids. **The second increment is
131	  `setActiveSystemPlanet('-1,-1:p1')`.**
132	- Of its two call sites, `EfficientScene.tsx:648` is unreachable here: its effect
133	  returns early while `controlMode === 'flight'` (`:622`) and unconditionally
134	  calls `setSystemLocationMode('surface')` at `:650` — the observed mode stayed
135	  `atmosphere`. **The executing call site is `ShipController.tsx:472-473`**, which
136	  also explains the stale-frame signature of the resulting state: a hearth-local
137	  pad pose published while `renderOrigin` still names Origin.
138	
139	Epoch 3→5 and 6→8 are therefore fully accounted: `+1` handoff, `+1` reclaim. The
140	37.2 s period is one full launch-and-cross, and `onOrigin()`
141	(`commonGroundDirector.ts:804-806`) is true only inside the unsampled sub-290 ms
142	window, in which the ship is nowhere near `CG_POSES.W`, so `tickReturn`'s landing
143	block (`:862-869`) can never fire and `story:ch13-origin-landed` stays false.
144	
145	## Smallest correction seam
146	
147	**One entry in one shipped table**, in the module that already documents this
148	class of bug:
149	
150	```ts
151	// main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts:128-131
152	'ch13-return': STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID
153	```
154	
155	Nothing else. Specifically it does **not** touch `resolveStoryBootWorldId`, so a
156	reload/Continue mid-crossing still restarts from the world the ship launched
157	from (the documented physical rule) — adding `ch13-return` to `originOwnedBeat`

# integration-handoff-standby — progress

Single integration engineer, sixth bounded material repair (CG-IMPL-012,
CG-IMPL-013). Governing documents read before any edit:
`handoff-standby-repair-direction.json`, `producer-handoff-standby-audit-review.json`,
`producer-focused-evidence-review.json`, `flight-discriminator-report.{json,md}`,
`handoff-standby-source-audit.{json,md}`, `producer-handoff-standby-budget-decision.json`,
`integration-inbox.md` (through the 15:45:02Z entry).

Not a creative lane. No plot, copy, geometry, proof, score or camera change. No
publication, no canonical gate/manifest/defect edit, no GPU work, no browser, no
destructive git of any kind (no checkout/restore/reset/stash/clean was run).

## Source ownership and byte preservation

Task-private exact-byte backups (outside `main/`, run-private):
`.private/handoff-standby-repair-backups/`.

| file | pre-repair sha256 |
|---|---|
| `main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts` | `e7237efcf339efb599222a171a22b0c4b118712025f3f777030c08482b7e103e` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.ts` | `980590b0add81f8e0ce6bdc182cb834940af336454435ff4d304a64e47ad11b5` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts` | `8379b552bd076c4311ba333182e7f0399e0b82a60093a16feddcdc0ed1fb8492` |
| `main/src/App.test.tsx` | absent (created by this repair) |

The first two match the read-only audit's recorded hashes, so the frozen dirty
source was the base. Every counterfactual below restored the exact pre-repair
bytes from those backups and the restored hash was verified against the
post-repair hash immediately afterwards.

**Path note.** `main/src/App.test.tsx` is one of the four commissioned paths but
did **not** exist on disk; the direction assumed it did. It was created rather
than routed, because it is an explicitly listed allowed path. No fifth path was
edited. Files outside the four paths were **read and imported only**
(`world/CommonGroundWorld.tsx` `createFooting`, `utils/agentSurfaceNavigation.ts`,
`utils/agentSurfaceNavigationRuntime.ts`, `story/autopilotSteering.ts`,
`state/systemFlight.ts`) — imports into an allowed test file, zero bytes changed.
Scratch lives only in `verifier/probes/handoff-standby-repair/` and
`logs/handoff-standby-repair/`; nothing temporary was created inside `main/src`.

## Task A — CG-IMPL-013, the ch13-return handoff reset

Accepted the producer's routing and the audit's executed reproduction. The
missing entry is restored in the existing runtime crossing table only:

```ts
// main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts
'ch13-return': STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID
```

`resolveStoryBootWorldId` is untouched, so a reload mid-crossing still restarts
from the world the ship launched from — arrival stays earned by flight. No boot
world change, no `SystemTravelDriver`/`ShipController`/state-reset change, no
teleport, no `targetReady` bypass, no radius/speed change, no milestone grant.

Regression: `main/src/App.test.tsx` (new, 10 tests). It drives the **real**
system-flight store through the **real** commit the app performs
(`commitSystemBodyTarget` → `commitSystemPlanetHandoff`, the `onMidpoint` body of
`beginPreparedSystemTargetHandoff`) and then evaluates App's own seam expression
(`App.tsx:537-545`) against the real resolver: post-handoff identity stable and
`storyWorldSwapPending` false; pre-handoff not early-origin; route offline and
mismatched current/active remain uncommitted; the measured reclaim
(`setActiveSystemPlanet` at `ShipController.tsx:472-473`) still un-commits;
ch8-crossing, ch10-ask and boot/Continue behaviour unchanged. No mocks.

Counterfactual: with the pre-repair `tidegardenRoute.ts` restored, exactly the
post-handoff assertion fails (`Expected "-1,-1" / Received "-1,-1:p1"`), 9 pass.
Bytes restored and re-verified.

## Task B — CG-IMPL-012, the standby stall

### Phase and candidate decision (published as root asked, with its rationale)

**Measured cause, reproduced before the patch was designed** (CPU, read-only,
`verifier/probes/handoff-standby-repair/standby-terrain-repro.mjs`, log
`logs/handoff-standby-repair/standby-terrain-repro.log`), on the actual world
identity — seed **3215739679**, world **-1,-1**, planetSize **50**,
`VOXEL_SCALE` 2, shipped generator, shipped `planAgentSurfaceRoute` with
`nextNavigationStep`'s own option set:

- `CG_STANDBY_CLEAR_OF_E = (-42, 51.05, 9)` is **over water**. Its cell
  `(-21, 25, 5)` has no solid column and `isWaterVoxel` is true. So is the
  lattice-aligned `(-42, ·, 10)`, and the whole `x = -42/-44` band south of the
  survey line. The audit's B1 (off-lattice) is therefore **not** the operative
  cause, and root's rejection of the "odd coordinate alone" claim is confirmed.
- From the measured stall pose `(-41.965326, 50.988996, 12.155896)` the shipped
  planner returns `requestedGoalWasWet: true`, `reason: already-at-resolved-goal`,
  `waypoints: 1`, resolved goal `z = 12` — the cell her body already occupied.
  That is the recorded `direct` / `stillTime 0` / `nudges 0` stall exactly, and
  it is B2 answered with a measurement rather than a hypothesis.

**Candidate qualification** (`standby-candidate-qualification.mjs`, log
alongside). Clearance is measured from polyline **SEGMENTS**, and includes the
**actual sampled offered route** — the 57 body samples the witness-2 hardware
trace recorded between `after-F-at-S` and `at-E-after-draw`, extracted to
`offered-route-witness2.json` — not static vertices:

| candidate | footing | recorded offer | LONG | SHORT | COMMON | E→H | W | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped `(-42,9)` | **false (water)** | 3.60 | 3.00 | 3.00 | 3.00 | 3.00 | 8.06 | rejected — no ground |
| audit `(-42,20)` | true | **0.30** | **0.00** | 8.00 | 2.83 | 8.00 | 12.81 | rejected — ON the long survey |
| audit `(-42,22)` | true | **0.46** | **0.00** | 10.00 | 4.47 | 10.00 | 14.42 | rejected — ON the long survey |
| authored `W` | true | 5.42 | 7.21 | **2.00** | 8.25 | 6.32 | **0.00** | rejected — it is HIS inspection pose, occupied at the moment the standby is needed, and only 2.0 off the short survey |
| authored `T` | true | 2.38 | 2.00 | 2.00 | 2.00 | 2.00 | 10.20 | rejected — his far reference, 2.0 from everything |
| `(-40,8)` | true | 4.89 | 4.47 | 4.00 | 4.47 | 4.00 | 6.32 | **qualifies** |
| `(-38,8)`, `(-36,6)`, `(-36,16)`, `(-30,8)`, `(-46,22)`, `(-48,22)` | true | ≥4.97 | ≥4.00 | ≥4.00 | ≥4.00 | ≥4.00 | ≥4.47 | qualify |

The producer's rejection of `(-42,20)/(-42,22)` is therefore reproduced
numerically: they are supported ground, they clear COMMON, and they sit exactly
on the span W-7744 is about to walk (0.30/0.46 from her actual recorded offer).
Authored `W` was checked rather than presumed and is **not** usable: it is his
occupied pose and it is 2.0 from the short survey — inside the required margin.

**Selected repair (chapter-local, `commonGroundDirector.ts` only).** The single
arithmetic constant is replaced by a *selection* over a small list of candidate
waiting places, all voxel-cell centres on the site's dry shelf, each confirmed
supported by the shipped footing over the real generator and reachable from S,
E, W and C by the shipped planner with `dry-surface-path` (never a substituted
goal). At runtime the nearest candidate wins that

1. the **live** footing supports (real terrain, not a fixture), and
2. clears, by `2 × BODY_BODY_CLEARANCE_UNITS + CG_RAIL_POSE_ARRIVE = 2.6`, the
   segments of every span he still has to walk: his current leg from where he
   actually stands through the untested remainder of the **recorded** samples,
   his positioning leg `E→H`, and `CG_ROUTE_COMMON` (which is also his
   independent test and the span she walks afterwards), plus his live body.

If nothing qualifies the rail publishes a **hold**, not a walk — the refusal is
surfaced, never hidden. Both existing call sites (survey stand-clear, common
positioning) share the one selection; the published reasons are unchanged.

What this does **not** touch: `CG_POSES`, `CG_ROUTE_SHORT/LONG/COMMON`,
`CG_LEG_*`, the 1-unit capsule/body clearance, the 0.6 standby arrival radius,
dry/cross-face/obstacle navigation safety, `agentSurfaceNavigation`,
`autopilot/primitives`, the exact-goal handoff, or any shared util. No bound was
widened, no body pose forced, no progress granted, no rescue enabled, no new F,
objective or target added for the player, and no required reference occupancy
removed.

Regression: 9 new tests in `commonGroundDirector.test.ts`, run against the REAL
`createFooting` over the real generator (earlier chapter tests used a flat
fixture plot that answers "supported" over water and would have passed on the
broken target) and the real planner: the stall reproduction; a supported and
genuinely reachable standby (`dry-surface-path`, >1 waypoint, resolved goal ==
requested target — not a cell substitution labelled "arrived"); segment
clearance of every span; explicit rejection of the two long-route candidates
even though they clear COMMON; an arbitrary **recorded** excursion that runs over
the preferred candidate, forcing selection elsewhere; the common-lane
positioning case; the honest hold when no ground qualifies; and the control that
W-7744 still holds for `body-clearance` when her body really is on his path and
releases only once she has actually moved.

Counterfactual: with the pre-repair `commonGroundDirector.ts` restored, 4 of the
9 fail (reachable standby, recorded span, common positioning, honest hold); the
reproduction and control tests pass either way, which is what they are for.
Bytes restored and re-verified.

## Evidence / limits

- Everything in Task B's terrain and planner work is a **CPU reconstruction** of
  terrain and navigation, plus the real vitest footing boundary. It is not a
  live proof and claims no GPU acceptance. The remaining physical gates are
  listed in the report.
- The recorded-offer polyline is the witness-2 body trace, which is the actual
  walked recording; the accepted route was 42 samples of the same walk.
- Ordering, stated plainly: the measurement and the candidate decision were made
  before any source edit; this progress file was written after the edits and
  before the final checks, at root's 15:45:02Z request.

occupied pose and it is 2.0 from the short survey — inside the required margin.

arithmetic constant is replaced by a *selection* over a small list of candidate
waiting places, all voxel-cell centres on the site's dry shelf, each confirmed
supported by the shipped footing over the real generator and reachable from S,
E, W and C by the shipped planner with `dry-surface-path` (never a substituted
goal). At runtime the nearest candidate wins that

1. the **live** footing supports (real terrain, not a fixture), and
2. clears, by `2 × BODY_BODY_CLEARANCE_UNITS + CG_RAIL_POSE_ARRIVE = 2.6`, the

   actually stands through the untested remainder of the **recorded** samples,
   his positioning leg `E→H`, and `CG_ROUTE_COMMON` (which is also his
   independent test and the span she walks afterwards), plus his live body.

If nothing qualifies the rail publishes a **hold**, not a walk — the refusal is
surfaced, never hidden. Both existing call sites (survey stand-clear, common
positioning) share the one selection; the published reasons are unchanged.

`CG_LEG_*`, the 1-unit capsule/body clearance, the 0.6 standby arrival radius,
dry/cross-face/obstacle navigation safety, `agentSurfaceNavigation`,

widened, no body pose forced, no progress granted, no rescue enabled, no new F,
objective or target added for the player, and no required reference occupancy
removed.

fixture plot that answers "supported" over water and would have passed on the
broken target) and the real planner: the stall reproduction; a supported and

clearance of every span; explicit rejection of the two long-route candidates

positioning case; the honest hold when no ground qualifies; and the control that

# Sixth bounded repair — CG-IMPL-013 (return handoff) and CG-IMPL-012 (standby stall)

Written **2026-09-06T15:53:10Z**. Integration engineer, single source owner.
Companion: `integration-handoff-standby-report.json`,
`integration-handoff-standby-progress.md`.

**Not an acceptance, not a defect closure, not a verification.** No publication.
No plot, copy, geometry, proof, score or camera change. No GPU or browser work.
No destructive git of any kind: `checkout`, `restore`, `reset`, `stash` and
`clean` were never invoked.

## What changed

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts` | `e7237efc…8482b7e103e` | `f35f6b16…44e504bf` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.ts` | `980590b0…4e47ad11b5` | `acc0d9cf…97166c46` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts` | `8379b552…0ed1fb8492` | `1b8e76af…cb11a97b` |
| `main/src/App.test.tsx` | *absent* (null) | `f19a1e4a…cbe7bd271` |

Post-repair rehash of the 98 manifest files: **95 matched, 3 changed, 0 missing,
0 unexpected drift**, aggregate `2d1ab0d2…199d8cb`. Nothing else in the tree was
modified. All other pre-existing dirty bytes are untouched, and the dirty tree —
not HEAD — was the restoration baseline throughout.

Tests: **3139 → 3158** (+19: 10 in `App.test.tsx`, 9 in
`commonGroundDirector.test.ts`), files **350 → 351**. Nothing removed, nothing
changed, nothing weakened.

## A — the ch13 return crossing

The measured reset was not the flight. The generic same-system handoff committed
every time; `main/src/story/tidegardenRoute.ts` simply did not list
`'ch13-return'` in the runtime crossing table, so one render later the resolver
still answered the departure world, App's swap effect reclaimed it and the ship
controller re-seated the ship on the hearth pad — the +2 activation epochs the
telemetry recorded (3→5, 6→8) after reaching 181.23 and 169.09 inside the 185
envelope.

One entry restored:

```ts
'ch13-return': STORY_PRIMARY_WORLD_ID
```

`resolveStoryBootWorldId` is deliberately untouched, so a reload mid-crossing
still restarts from the hearth: **arrival stays earned by flying**. No boot-world
change, no driver/controller/state-reset change, no teleport, no `targetReady`
bypass, no radius or speed change, no granted milestone.

`main/src/App.test.tsx` (new) drives the **real** flight store through the real
`commitSystemBodyTarget` → `commitSystemPlanetHandoff` the app performs, then
evaluates App's own seam expression with the real resolver: post-handoff stable;
pre-handoff not early-origin; offline route uncommitted; mismatched
current/active uncommitted in both directions; the measured second mutator still
un-commits; ch8, ch10, non-crossing beats and reload/Continue unchanged.
**Counterfactual:** restoring the pre-repair table fails exactly the post-handoff
assertion (`Expected "-1,-1" / Received "-1,-1:p1"`), 9 others pass; bytes
restored and hash-verified.

## B — the standby

**Reproduced before touching source.** On the actual identity (seed
**3215739679**, world `-1,-1`, planetSize **50**, `VOXEL_SCALE` 2), the shipped
standby `(-42, 51.05, 9)` is **over water** — its cell has no solid column and
`isWaterVoxel` is true — and so is the lattice-aligned `(-42, ·, 10)`. From the
exact stall pose the shipped planner returns `requestedGoalWasWet: true`,
`already-at-resolved-goal`, **one** waypoint, resolved `z = 12`: the cell she was
already standing in. That is the recorded `direct` / `stillTime 0` / `nudges 0`
freeze, exactly. The off-lattice theory is **not** the cause.

**The audit's proposal is rejected on measurement, as root required.**
`(-42,20)` and `(-42,22)` are good ground and clear of COMMON — and they are
`0.00` from the LONG survey and `0.30` / `0.46` from her **actual recorded
offer**. They are on the span he is about to walk. Authored `W` was checked, not
presumed, and also fails: it is his occupied inspection pose and only `2.00` off
the short survey. `T` is his far reference and `2.00` from everything.

The repair is chapter-local and lives only where the old constant did. The
standby is now **selected** at runtime: the nearest candidate that the **live**
footing supports and that clears — from polyline **segments** — his current leg
through the untested remainder of the **recorded** samples, his `E→H`
positioning leg, `CG_ROUTE_COMMON` (also his independent test, and her own later
traversal) and his live body, by `2 × 1 + 0.6 = 2.6` units. Candidates are cell
centres on the dry shelf, each measured supported and reachable by the shipped
planner as a real `dry-surface-path` walk whose resolved goal *is* the request —
not a substitution labelled "arrived". **If nothing qualifies, the rail holds**
with a null target; the refusal is published, not hidden.

Untouched: `CG_POSES`, all three routes, the positioning legs, the 1-unit body
clearance, the 0.6 standby arrival, the 0.35 route arrival, cross-face/dry/
obstacle safety, `agentSurfaceNavigation`, `autopilot/primitives`, the exact-goal
handoff and every shared util. Nothing granted, nothing forced, no rescue, no
endpoint pumping, no new player action, no change to the witness/reference
occupancy, and no touch to CG-IMPL-009 or the ordered 18-unit proof.

Nine regressions run the **real** `createFooting` over the real generator —
every earlier chapter test used a flat fixture plot that answers "supported" over
water and would have passed on the broken target — plus the real planner, the
real actor walk and hold, and an arbitrary recorded excursion that forces the
selection to move. **Counterfactual:** restoring the pre-repair director fails 4
of the 9; the reproduction and the body-clearance control pass in both states by
design; bytes restored and hash-verified.

## Checks

`npm --prefix main run verify`, cwd `/home/thomasphillip/Projects/vox`, **exit
0** — 351 files / 3158 tests passed, build succeeded. Log
`logs/handoff-standby-repair/verify.log`, sha256
`54a473d489deff9e73bc8c1379955e31684907f1fb773eb3de0e6ecd765d7fa0`. The story,
registry, journey, authority, guidance/UX and scene-AV checks are the named
package scripts inside that one composite command; they were not re-invoked
separately and nothing was re-run without a change or a failure.

## Limits and what is still owed

Everything above is CPU: the real generator, the real footing, the real planner
and the real flight store under vitest. **No GPU acceptance is claimed.**
Still independently required, and none of it by me:

- a fresh headed capture of ch13-return: epoch **+1**, `activePlanetId`
  *staying* the origin, `renderOrigin [0,0,0]`, no jump back to the pad, no
  second 37.2 s cycle, and an actual landing — with ch8/ch10 and reload controls;
- a physical survey capture in which the standby is genuinely walked inside the
  unchanged 0.6 radius;
- the COMMON 18-unit ordered passage in a browser (CG-IMPL-009 remains
  unmeasured);
- lawful earned Continue, full story/station, AV variants, and the independent
  chapter reviews.

One boundary item for root's record: `main/src/App.test.tsx` was listed as an
allowed path but did not exist; it was created, not substituted, and no unlisted
path was edited.

Source is frozen at the hashes above. No gate compilation, defect closure or
review was performed here.

Done. One bounded repair, both defects, source frozen.

## What I did

**A — CG-IMPL-013 (measured Origin handoff reset).** The generic same-system handoff was always committing; `CROSSING_DESTINATION_WORLD_ID` in `tidegardenRoute.ts` just never listed `ch13-return`, so one render later the resolver still answered the departure world, App's swap effect reclaimed it and the ship was re-seated on the hearth pad (+2 epochs per attempt). Restored the one entry. `resolveStoryBootWorldId` is untouched — a reload mid-crossing still restarts from the hearth, so arrival stays earned by flight. New `main/src/App.test.tsx` (10 tests) drives the **real** flight store through the real `commitSystemPlanetHandoff` and evaluates App's own seam expression: post-handoff stable, pre-handoff not early-origin, offline/mismatched uncommitted, the measured reclaim still un-commits, ch8/ch10/boot controls unchanged. Counterfactual: pre-repair bytes fail exactly the post-handoff assertion.

**B — CG-IMPL-012 (standby stall).** Reproduced on CPU *before* editing, on the actual identity (seed 3215739679, world -1,-1, planet 50, voxel 2): `(-42,51.05,9)` is **over water**, and so is the lattice-aligned `(-42,·,10)` — so the planner returned `requestedGoalWasWet`, substituted her own cell, `already-at-resolved-goal`, one waypoint. That is the freeze; the off-lattice theory is not the cause. The audit's `(-42,20/22)` measure **0.00** from LONG and **0.30/0.46** from her actual recorded 57-sample offer — rejected numerically, as root required. Authored `W` was checked, not presumed, and also fails (his occupied pose, 2.00 off the short survey). Replaced the arithmetic constant with a chapter-local **selection**: nearest candidate the live footing supports that clears, by segments, his current leg through the untested recorded samples, `E→H`, the common route and his body, by 2.6 units — and an honest hold when none qualifies. No signed pose/route, clearance, arrival radius, shared nav or agency change. 9 regressions run the **real** `createFooting` over the real generator (every earlier chapter test used a flat fixture that answers "supported" over water); 4 fail on pre-repair bytes.

**Checks:** `npm --prefix main run verify`, cwd repo root, **exit 0**, 351 files / **3158** tests (baseline 3139, +19, none removed/changed); log SHA recorded. Rehash: 95/98 unchanged, exactly the 3 commissioned game-source paths changed, zero drift; all counterfactuals restored byte-exact; no destructive git; no GPU.

**Two things for your attention:** `main/src/App.test.tsx` was listed as an allowed path but did not exist — I created it rather than expanding scope, and recorded that. And no GPU acceptance is claimed: the fresh headed ch13-return capture, the walked-standby capture, and the COMMON 18-unit browser proof remain independent gates.
